clue.text: Its leaf on wee statuette?

parts.note: a statue's modesty is traditionally covered by a fig leaf, so its leaf is a fig
wee is informal British for urine

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at a little statue and the leaf stuck on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' looks like Scottish for small, describing the statuette; it is the noun for urine. 'Its leaf' is the fig leaf that covers classical statues.
explanation.definitionFit: A small modelled human or animal figure is a statuette, the ornament sense of the word.

clue.text: Frequency with which US sect starve

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for frequency
the Amish are a religious sect in the US

explanation.surface: How often an American religious group goes hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish is to suffer or cause extreme hunger, an old verb sense matching starve.

clue.text: Swiss banker invests energy in complete set of personal make-up

indicators.note: invests here means clothes or surrounds, so the banker word wraps around the energy letter

parts.note: the gnomes of Zurich is a nickname for Swiss bankers
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A Swiss financier putting energy into a full cosmetics kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' suggests cosmetics but means genetic constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: The full set of genetic material in an organism, its personal biological constitution.

clue.text: Big beast's tail bitten off by antelope in demilitarised zone once

indicators.note: tail bitten off means the beast's last letter is removed

parts.note: a rhino is a big beast
an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A wildlife scene of a rhinoceros attacked by an antelope in a buffer zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The German region west of the river was demilitarised after the First World War until Hitler reoccupied it in 1936.

clue.text: Dismissal of cop — canteen can go wild

indicators.note: go wild means the letters run riot and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman is sacked and the canteen descends into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to accept something is to dismiss it, so rejection is the shared sense.

clue.text: Like many cathedrals, become almost intimate

parts.note: to go can mean to become, as in 'go mad'

indicators.note: almost means the word for intimate is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: people who are very close are said to be thick with each other

explanation.surface: Someone describing a growing closeness as being like a great church.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed-arch medieval architectural style used for many European cathedrals is called Gothic.

clue.text: Please speed to airport

parts.note: O is an exclamation of entreaty, as in 'O, please'
to hare is to run very fast

explanation.surface: A traveller begging to rush to catch a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago's main international airport bears this name, after a naval aviator.

clue.text: Joint request to include fluid in this?

definitions.text: Joint request to include fluid in this?

parts.note: the hip is a joint
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Asking for a drink to be poured into a small pocket container.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat container for spirits, carried in a hip pocket, which holds the fluid asked for.

clue.text: Crown and Church join in dirge

parts.note: corona is Latin for crown

explanation.surface: Monarchy and church unite in a funeral song.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronach is a Scottish or Irish funeral lament, a song of mourning.

clue.text: Opera is back in the big house

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the opera's name

parts.note: Manon is an opera by Massenet

indicators.note: back means the little word is is written in reverse order

explanation.surface: A performance returns to a stately home venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansion is a large, grand residence, so it is a fitting synonym for the big house.

clue.text: Cover popular artist's sound

indicators.note: sound signals that the artist's title is to be heard rather than spelt, giving a word with a silent W

parts.note: a rapper is a popular music artist

explanation.surface: Someone recording a cover version of a pop star's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a cover version of a song, but it is a noun for a protective covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is a covering of paper or film put around something, so it is a cover.

clue.text: Point at which inexpert actor joined players

parts.note: west is a compass point
a ham is an overacting, poor actor
united means joined

explanation.surface: A clumsy actor joining a theatre company at some juncture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' suggests actors, matching the surface, but means a team. WEST HAM UNITED is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A football club is a team of players, so the club's name stands for a set of players.

clue.text: Wine waiters lose half the battle

indicators.note: lose half means only the first five of the ten letters of the wine waiters' title are kept

parts.note: sommeliers are wine waiters in restaurants

explanation.surface: Restaurant staff struggling, losing half their fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme was the First World War battle of 1916 on the French river of that name.

clue.text: For one running keep tin of beer?

indicators.note: a tin of beer contains beer, so of puts the beer inside the tin

parts.note: a can is a tin
Stella Artois is a well-known lager, called Stella for short

explanation.surface: Someone who jogs keeping a can of lager handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' and 'keep' read as a jogger holding on to something; a keep is the strong tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A castellan is the governor or warden of a castle, in charge of the fortress and its keep.

clue.text: Bravely handle consequences of awful cafe and what's piped into it?

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of cafe are badly arranged and need reworking

parts.note: piped music is what gets played into a cafe through speakers

explanation.surface: Putting up with a dreadful cafe and its background music.
explanation.definitionFit: To face the music is an idiom for accepting criticism or punishment for one's actions with courage.

clue.text: Pygmy militia member?

definitions.meaning: a tiny person might be read as a ...
in the American Revolution, militiamen ready to fight at a minute's notice had this name

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it describes a tiny person; as one it is an American revolutionary soldier.

clue.text: Party official meets Leader of House with advantage

parts.note: a whip enforces party discipline in Parliament

indicators.note: Leader of means take only the opening letter of House

parts.note: and means with, joining things

explanation.surface: A parliamentary enforcer meets the Leader of the House to gain the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the controlling position over someone, an idiom for the upper hand or advantage.

clue.text: Raised support to translate Torah for Scots community

indicators.note: raised means the support word is read upwards, from bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: a bra is a support garment

indicators.note: to translate here means to change the letters of Torah into a new order

explanation.surface: Help is offered to render Hebrew scripture for a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: ARBROATH is a fishing town on the east coast of Scotland, famous for its smokies.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Angus, Scotland, which is a community.

clue.text: Passable property of woman to change, possessing boring name

parts.note: her refers to a woman

indicators.note: possessing means the word for change holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: to edit is to change a text
tame means dull or boring

explanation.surface: A woman altering an estate that is tediously described.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term for any property that can be inherited, which is what passable means here: able to be passed on.

clue.text: A condition causing swelling on one rodent

parts.note: gout is a disease causing swollen joints
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An animal suffering from a swollen ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged burrowing rodent of Central and South America, related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Erotic, like a Turkish bath

definitions.meaning: a Turkish bath is full of hot vapour

explanation.surface: Someone describing a sensual scene set in a sauna.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the racy sense and the vapour-filled sense are uses of the same adjective.

clue.text: Perhaps chicken wing and leg found on top of Capital Hill

definitions.text: found on top of Capital Hill

parts.note: a chicken wing is, for example, part of a hen, read as PART and HEN
leg is the on side in cricket, giving ON

explanation.surface: A menu of chicken pieces served on a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital Hill' echoes Washington's Capitol Hill; here it is the hill in the capital, Athens. Leg side and on side are the same half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: The temple to Athena stands on the Acropolis, the hill at the centre of the Greek capital.

clue.text: Bird of paradise?

parts.note: bird is slang for a young woman, and in Islamic tradition beautiful maidens await the faithful in paradise

explanation.definitionFit: A beautiful virgin of the Muslim paradise, read cryptically as a heavenly young woman.

clue.text: Mean to get drunk

definitions.meaning: a stingy person is ... with money

explanation.surface: Someone means to get intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the miserly sense and the tipsy sense are everyday informal uses of the same adjective.

clue.text: Usually like beer, which sport interferes with

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: interferes with means the sport gets in among the letters of the beer

parts.note: ale is a beer
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Someone saying beer is normally spoilt by the games on television.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase meaning generally or normally, a fixed idiom equal to usually.

clue.text: King left upmarket version of fried fish

indicators.note: left means the king's letter departs from the letters of upmarket
version of means the remaining letters are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch walking out on a posh take on fish and chips.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove K from UPMARKET, leaving UPMARET, then rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese dish of seafood or vegetables fried in light batter, often prawns or fish.

clue.text: Hard to impress surrealist with a flower

indicators.note: to impress here means to press into, so the letter for hard is set inside the painter's name

parts.note: Salvador Dali was a surrealist painter
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: It's tough to win over a surrealist painter using a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plant with showy blooms, named after the Swedish botanist Anders Dahl.

clue.text: I had existence as a distinct personality

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
entity means being or existence

explanation.surface: Someone reflecting that they once lived as a separate individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's sense of self, the characteristics that make them a separate individual.
